p.i: stra, inquam, cùm in alios cŏplu-res, tum in illum ingrata Gallia, jampridem vidit. Sic autem ille observationibus istis nostris delectabatur, quinetiā ita libēter quæ nō placebant meo rogatu emēdabat, vt iā tum illarum à me promulgationē[?] exposceret: præsertim propter nouas hominum quorūdam opiniones, q juventute ab Aristotelis præcepit: revocabāt: quorū ille se rationibus atque institutis infestissimū semper præbuit. Post vero intermissis ciuilibus latrociniis cùm illas easdem obseruationes meas Lutetiam ad exercitatissimos Dialecticos emēdandi, siquid vellet, caussa misis-sem, eásque ipsis mirificè probari

page.notes: Uncertain readings: "promulgationē[?]" (the abbreviation mark after "mulgatio" is faint; the word is likely promulgationem). "revocabāt" is printed with a letter that could be "n" for "v"; the reading follows the sense. The first word on the page is a fragment, "stra", with its beginning cut off, and it is transcribed as such. The page carries no printed page number; the only mark at the foot right is the signature "ʃ 3", transcribed as "s 3[?]". Long s is written as plain s throughout, and the ligature "ct" in "delectabatur" is read as ct. The accents and macrons are transcribed as printed.
